explanation: The hull holds the steam until the pressure bursts it and the starch puffs into foam. Sweetcorn kernels have more porous hulls that let steam leak out, so they rarely pop.

claims.text: A popcorn kernel bursts when water inside it turns to steam and the pressure ruptures its hull.
Popcorn does not pop because of expanding trapped air, oil soaking in or sugar caramelizing.
When popcorn pops, the starch inside softens and puffs into a foam that sets as it cools.
Sweetcorn kernels have more porous hulls that let steam escape, so they rarely pop.

issues.note: c4: no Tier A or B source found for sweetcorn hulls being more porous (the search returned only Tier C pages). Drop the sentence, or soften it, or support it with a cereal chemistry source.

evidence.restatement: Popcorn pops because its hull is unusually strong and nearly moisture-tight, so steam builds until it bursts. Other kinds of corn lose more moisture through the hull and pop poorly. For sweetcorn in particular, the sugary, low-starch kernel (shrivelled when dry) is also part of the story, so I cannot say with certainty that a more porous hull is why it rarely pops.
